\(GW_0=W_0+(G-I)W_0\), so it is LoRA-FA with frozen \(A_0=W_0\) (unfolded, \(C\times9C\)), pointed at \(B=0\). FourierFT's image lies in the point-symmetric subspace DeltaW_{j,l}=DeltaW_{-j,-l}; wavelet atoms are not point-symmetric.

Im SVFT is not inside Im SVDiff = {U diag(s) V^T : s>=0}: SVFT^P reaches negative coefficients sigma_i+m_i<0 and off-diagonal Omega reaches non-spectral directions. The converse inclusion Im SVDiff in Im SVFT^P does hold (m=ReLU(sigma+delta)-sigma, checked to 2e-15), but only set-level: that h is not smooth, so it is not an arrow of Meth.
SVFT^P (diagonal Omega) reaches rank min(m,n), above r.
Same U Sigma_i V^T core form, but FacT trains shared U,V: d(FacT)=2dr+12Lr^2-2r^2 exceeds d(LoRA-XS on 12L boxes)=12Lr^2, and LoRA-XS's frames are W_i's frozen SVD frames.
NOLA's row space moves inside span{A_i} while VeRA's is fixed at row A; with dense random bases neither image contains the other.
A generic SAID update restricted to one weight matrix is a dense random vector \(P_j\theta'\) reshaped, of full rank, so its maximum rank exceeds r.
Both are a single global random projection, but Uni-LoRA projects into LoRA factor space (every matrix update has rank at most r) while SAID's per-matrix updates are generically full rank.

VeRA embeds in Tied-LoRA by A2 (freeze \(A,B\); re-point \(u_0\) from 1 to VeRA's 0.1), but not back: \(d(\mathrm{TL6})=r(d_{in}+d_{out})+L(d_{out}+r)-(d_{out}+2r+L-1)\) exceeds VeRA's \(L(d_{out}+r-1)\) by \(r(d_{in}+d_{out})-d_{out}-2r+1>0\).
\(A\) is trained, so the shared row space leaves \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0\); LoRA-FA\((A_0)\) is only the A-frozen sub-object, and that arrow goes the other way (A2).

ShareA's free per-layer \(B_\ell\) give \(d=L\,d_{out}r+r\,d_{in}-r^2\), while Tied-LoRA's per-layer freedom is diagonal: \(d(\mathrm{ShareA})-d(\text{Tied-LoRA})=(r-1)\big[(d_{out}-1)(L-1)-r\big]>0\) for \(r\ge2\) once \((d_{out}-1)(L-1)>r\) [Num: 42 vs 34, 30 vs 28].

No arrow into \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r'}\) for \(r'<r\): PRoLoRA's generic rank is r [Num]. In particular the LoRA of equal budget has rank \(r_{\rm eq}=\big[u(d_{in}+d_{out})+(r-u)(d_{in}/m+d_{out}/n)\big]/(d_{in}+d_{out})<r\) for \(m,n\ge2\), \(u<r\).

MiSS's update \(D(\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_r)\) keeps its row space inside the fixed space \(\mathrm{row}(\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_r)\); PRoLoRA's unshared ranks \(B_uA_u\) have arbitrary row spaces, although both tile shards.
Tied-LoRA keeps every layer's row space inside the common \(\mathrm{row}\,A\) (an invariant of its image); MoS with private shards and random subsets gives layer-specific row spaces.
Against \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) at the same r, RaSA's per-layer maximum rank \(r-k+Lk>r\) (for \(L\ge2,k\ge1\)) is out of reach.
VeRA's updates have row and column spaces in frozen random frames, LoRA-XS's in the top-r SVD frames of \(W_0\); the two images meet only at \(\theta_0\) generically.
MiCA uses the minor left singular vectors, LoRA-XS the top ones, so column spaces are orthogonal and the images meet only at \(\theta_0\).
The early phase moves in \(m\,r\) dimensions, far more than LoRA-XS's \(r^2\). Only the U-frozen sub-object is LoRA-XS-like, and if U moved early its frame is \(U'\ne U_r\), not the SVD frame.
Random outer frames versus the SVD frames of \(W_0\): \(\mathrm{col}\,P\not\subseteq\mathrm{span}\,U_r\) generically, so the images meet only at \(\theta_0\).
A balanced random tessellation gives generically full-rank updates, so the maximum rank exceeds r.
SHiRA's image leaves \(W_0\) unchanged off its mask; MoSA moves every entry.
C3A ties entries along block-circulant diagonals, MoSA along a random partition. These are two different tying subspaces, which meet only at \(\theta_0\) generically.

FourierFT's image lies in the point-symmetric subspace \(\Delta W_{j,l}=\Delta W_{-j,-l}\) (Prop II.13). A Hartley pattern has a nonzero point-antisymmetric (sine) part unless its frequency is self-conjugate (\((0,0)\), \((m/2,0)\), \((0,n/2)\), \((m/2,n/2)\)), so Im SSH is not contained in Im FourierFT for any support with a non-self-conjugate frequency.
Hartley versus DCT-II frames: sparse supports in two different orthogonal frames give subspaces that meet only at \(\theta_0\) generically.
DCT-II basis matrices are not point-symmetric modulo \((m,n)\), so they leave FourierFT's point-symmetric image.

Since \(C,D\) are orthogonal, \(\operatorname{rank}\Delta W=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal S(a,l)\), which for generic coefficients is the term rank (maximum matching) of the support pattern. At the matched budget \(\mathcal B\approx r(d_{in}+d_{out})\) random locations give term rank close to \(\min(m,n)>r\); \(d=\mathcal B>r(m+n-r)\) also exceeds LoRA's dimension.

For generic parameters Compacter's box function \(h+U\,\mathrm{GeLU}(Dh)\) is non-affine in \(h\), so its functional image is not contained in that of the weight-space Kronecker-sum update KAdaptation (M1), even though both use the same LPHM parametrisation.
Same reason: only with \(\sigma=\mathrm{id}\) would the adapter be a linear insertion comparable to LoRA (Prop VI.4).

Against \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) at the same r, \(\rho_{\max}=kr>r\). Conversely \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) does not map into GraLoRA, because a generic rank-r update has rank r on every block; the images are incomparable (Prop II.12(c)).
MELoRA's image keeps every off-diagonal block at zero (an absolute invariant) and GraLoRA fills them. MELoRA to GraLoRA is the A2 arrow, not the reverse.
\(\rho_{\max}=r\,\mathrm{rk}W_0>r\).
(IA)\(^3\) maps into \(\mathrm{HiRA}_1\) (A3), but not back: \(d(\mathrm{HiRA}_r)=r(m+n-r)>m\).
\(\mathrm{LoHa}_{r_1,r_2}\) does not map into \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r'}\) for \(r'<\min(r_1r_2,m,n)\) (generic rank \(r_1r_2\)).

HiRA's image keeps every zero of \(W_0\) (Prop II.9(e)), while LoHa's update does not depend on \(W_0\) and fills them. For \(W_0\) without zeros, \(\mathrm{Im\,HiRA}_r=W_0\odot\mathcal M_{\le r}\), and a generic LoHa update divided entrywise by a generic \(W_0\) has full rank [Num: rank 10 of 10 already for \(\mathrm{LoHa}_{1,1}\)], so \(\mathrm{Im\,LoHa}\not\subseteq\mathrm{Im\,HiRA}_r\) for every \(r<\min(m,n)\).
\(\mathrm{LoKr}_{r'}\) does not map into \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) when \(r<\min(u_p,u_q)\,r'\): the maximum rank exceeds r (Thm II.11(e)).
A 1-2% mask that includes a diagonal reaches full rank, so \(\rho_{\max}>r\).

MELoRA keeps the off-diagonal blocks at zero. BD-LoRA's row block i is \(B_iA^{(i)}\) over all input columns, so it fills them. The reverse map MELoRA \(\to\) BD-LoRA is the inclusion of block-diagonal \(A\); it is pointed (an A2 sub-object) only when BD-LoRA is pointed at a block-diagonal \(A_0\), since its default Gaussian \(A_0\) has nonzero off-diagonal parts.

BOFT is an action method that preserves |cos| between neurons (and the Gram structure up to its output scale); Quantum-PEFT is additive and changes spectra, although both build orthogonal matrices from Kronecker-structured factors.
SHiRA's image leaves \(W_0\) unchanged off its mask, while RoSA's low-rank summand moves every entry.
The mask summand reaches full rank, so \(\rho_{\max}>r\).

\(d(\mathrm{ABBA})=\min(mn,r_1(m+n-r_1)+r_2(m+n-r_2)-(m+n-1))\) (LoHa's count, an equality checked numerically, Prop II.12) exceeds \(d(\mathrm{HiRA}_{r_2})=r_2(m+n-r_2)\) once \(r_1\ge2\). HiRA fixes the first factor at \(W_0\); ABBA only starts near it. More strongly, for generic \(W_0\) a LoHa-type update divided entrywise by \(W_0\) has full rank [Num], so \(\mathrm{Im\,ABBA}\not\subseteq\mathrm{Im\,HiRA}_r\) for every \(r<\min(m,n)\).

Against LoHa at HF's default pointing (Kaiming \(B_1,A_1,B_2\), zero \(A_2\)=hada_w2_b): \(S_1(\mathrm{ABBA})=\{[W_0]_{r_1}\odot XA_2^0\}\) is not contained in \(S_1(\mathrm{LoHa})=\{B_1^0A_1^0\odot B_2^0Y\}\) for generic random factors, so there is no pointed arrow despite equal images.

\(\rho_{\max}=\mathrm{rk}A\cdot\mathrm{rk}B\) (\(I_d\) has Kronecker rank 1 and rank d) exceeds r. Conversely a generic rank-one update has Kronecker rank \(\kappa_1\) (Thm II.11(c)), so \(\mathrm{LoRA}_1\) does not map into KronA either.
Per-adapter slow weights and full-rank fast weights give \(d(\mathrm{PHM})\gg d(\mathrm{Compacter})\) (shared \(A_i\), rank-\(\rho\) fast weights); Compacter to PHM is the A3 arrow.
Its box function is non-affine (GeLU), so its functional image is not inside that of any weight-space method such as KAdaptation.

Cut-rank across the Kronecker cut: for the same \(n\times n\) split, LoKr's update \(C\otimes BA\) has Kronecker rank 1 (Thm II.11(a)), while KAdaptation's sum of n terms has Kronecker rank up to n. The framework files Kronecker-rank obstructions under O2 (axes.json O2 examples).
Compacter sits after the sublayer and cannot change attention scores at its own layer, whereas KAdaptation edits \(W_q,W_k\); the functional images are incomparable.
With the matched output split, \(d(\mathrm{KRAdapter})=(k_1+k_2-1)d_{in}\) exceeds \(d(\mathrm{KronA})=a_1a_2+b_1b_2-1\) (\(a_2b_2=d_{in}\)), and KronA's update has Kronecker rank 1.
Against LoRA at its standard \(T_A\) pointing: LoRETTA's base point is a smooth point of a translated cone and LoRA's is an apex, and the images are incomparable (Thm II.2(d)).
TT-LoRA starts from an uncompensated Gaussian \(\Delta W_0\) (a defect), LoRETTA from a compensated split. The base points differ, so there is no pointed arrow even where the images nest.
TT-LoRA's base point carries an uncompensated defect; LoRETTA compensates its random product (a split). Different base points, so no pointed arrow.
LoTR's per-(layer, family) cores are free (\(|\mathcal W|r^2\) dimensions) while MetaTT's factorise as \(G_2[l]G_3[m]\) (\((L+M)r^2\)), so \(d(\mathrm{LoTR})>d(\mathrm{MetaTT})\).
LoTR trains its shared, randomly initialised frames, so column and row spaces leave each layer's top-r SVD frames, which LoRA-XS keeps frozen.
The trainable A, B leave the frozen SVD frames. Only the sub-object with A, B frozen is a (random-frame) generalised LoRA-XS.
VeRA is read as a CP model with frozen factors (LoRTA Sec. 3), so arrows go from frozen-frame CP into LoRTA. LoRTA trains its frames and leaves VeRA's frozen random row and column spaces.
MetaTT's \(r\times r\) cores are general and LoRTA's diagonal, so \(d(\mathrm{MetaTT})-d(\mathrm{LoRTA})\approx(L+M)(r^2-r)>0\). Only LoRTA to MetaTT-5D exists.
A connected gate circuit reaches full rank (its min-cut avoids an r-bottleneck), while the maximum rank of LoRA_r is r.
The rank of I (x) M reaches (d/r_hat) r_hat = d > r; conversely LoRA does not map to MoRA (O1), since a generic rank-one update is not block-tied.
MoRA's maximum rank (up to d) exceeds MELoRA_r's maximum rank r.
MoRA ties all diagonal blocks to one M, so a block-diagonal update with distinct blocks is not in Im MoRA.
The shuffle P_2 couples off-diagonal blocks, which MELoRA's block-diagonal image never reaches (MELoRA is MoRe with P_1 = P_2 = I, a different object).
Against \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) at equal rank: the maximum rank \(r+c\) exceeds \(r\). (The arrow above lands in \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r+c}\).)

Generically, at comparable LoRA rank, Im DSEE is not contained in Im RoSA unless Omega lies inside RoSA's gradient mask (DSEE's support comes from robust PCA of W_0). The obstruction needs that rank condition: if RoSA's rank exceeds r by at least |Omega minus mask|, each off-mask entry is absorbed as a rank-one term and the inclusion holds.
The rank of sin(omega BA)/g grows with omega beyond r; conversely LoRA does not map to Sine-LoRA (O1), since Sine-LoRA never leaves |Delta W_ij| <= 1/g.
boft_s rescales neurons, while exact OFT preserves K_out = W W^T (Cor II.6).
Full-depth BOFT(log2 d, 2) has (d/2) log2 d angles plus a scale, so d(BOFT) > d(GOFT) = d - 1.
Against LoRA's default T_A pointing (0, A_0): S_1(DEFT) = {P_0 Y} and S_1(LoRA) = {X A_0} are incomparable, so neither simulates the other despite equal images (Thm II.2(a)).
PaRa has no base point over theta_0, so only the weak morphism B -> (B, 0) into DEFT exists (its image lies in W_0 + M_{<=r}).

ETHER's image is a compact set of reflections W_0 H^B inside W_0 O(n): it excludes theta_0 and preserves K_out, which DeLoRA's additive updates change. DeLoRA is derived from ETHER, but neither simulates the other.

The W_0 (.) A path alone reaches rank min(m, n, r rank W_0), generically full rank (the rank of a Hadamard product is at most the product of the ranks). That is beyond LoRA_r, and beyond LoRA_{2r} at the same budget.

HRA reaches rotations with eigenvalue -1 (e.g. H_{e1} H_{e2}), which the Cayley map never produces; for block OFT its moved planes also break the partial Grams (Thm II.7(d)). The eigenvalue argument is at image level for injective W_0 (out_features >= in_features), the setting of Thm II.7.
The rank of diag(l - 1) W_0 reaches rank W_0 > r; conversely LoRA does not map to (IA)^3 (O1).
Scales change neuron norms, which exact OFT preserves.
RoAd_1 ties the scale within each rotated output pair, so independent scalings of the two rows of a pair lie outside Im RoAd_1 (they lie in RoAd_2/4).
LN-gain edits act as column scalings of the consuming boxes (and move different coordinates of Theta), not as bias translations; neither image contains the other.
HF's Cayley-Neumann R = C(Q)(I - Q^4) is orthogonal only when Q^4 has eigenvalues in {0, 2}, so near theta_0 the two images meet only at theta_0.
rank(R - I) reaches n > r.
Cayley-Neumann images are not orthogonal (R^T R = (I - Q^4)^2), so they change K_out; near theta_0 the images of OFT and OFTv2 meet only at theta_0.

OSF moves only the minor block U_perp (x) V_perp, PSOFT only the principal block U_r (x) V_r: near theta_0 the images meet only at theta_0. This needs PSOFT's rank r <= effective_rank e, so that PSOFT's principal block lies inside OSF's frozen top block.
alpha, beta change the principal singular values, which Spectral Adapter^R preserves; only at alpha = beta = 1 is PSOFT a one-sided Spectral Adapter^R.
The scalings change K_out, and even at alpha = beta = 1 the rotation of the principal input subspace is not block-aligned, so it breaks OFT's partial Grams.
Pair rotations move row lines, which (IA)^3 fixes while its scales are non-zero.
The alpha_i rescale neuron pairs and change K_out; OFT acts on the input side and preserves it.
Output rescalings diag(mu) W_0 have rank up to rank W_0, outside LoRA_r's image (axes.json O1 example).
DeLoRA's image is LoRA's cone, which misses DoRA's output rescalings; DeLoRA normalises the update, DoRA the weight.
GOFT's layers couple coordinates across OFT's blocks (breaking its partial Grams) and can produce eigenvalue -1, which exact Cayley never does.
Non-conformal blocks change neuron norms and angles, which GOFT's rotations preserve.
BOFT preserves |cos| between neurons (Cor II.6 remarks), qGOFT does not.
ETHER is unpointed: for an even number n of blocks its image lies in Im HRA_n (n reflections with disjoint supports), but only through a weak morphism, never a pointed one.
Reflections have eigenvalue -1, which the Cayley map never produces.
The factors I - uu^T + vv^T are not orthogonal (singular when u is orthogonal to v), so ETHER+ changes K_out (Cor II.6 remarks).
ETHER's image consists of exact block reflections and excludes theta_0; ETHER+ reaches theta_0 and non-orthogonal matrices.
SVDiff moves singular values with frames fixed, Spectral Adapter^R moves frames with values fixed: near theta_0 the images meet only at theta_0.
The left rotation R_U changes K_out = W W^T, which input-side OFT preserves.

At equal rank \(r\), against LoRA's Type I apex: a Type II smooth point, and the images are incomparable (Thm II.2(d)), so there is no arrow either way at that rank. (Via PiSSA it does map into \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{2r}\) at a degenerate pointing, Thm II.1.)
SVDiff changes singular values with fixed frames, while Spectral Adapter^R preserves the spectrum.
z_i < 0 flips the sign of sigma_i u_i v_i^T, which SVDiff's ReLU(sigma + delta) >= 0 never reaches; the two agree only as germs at theta_0.
As DoRA: output rescalings lie outside LoRA_r's image.
The shift beta and the scaling of every output channel (including the outputs of W_up) lie outside (IA)^3's image.
RED scales the output side of W_down (and shifts it), (IA)^3 its input side: {diag(l) W} and {W diag(l')} meet only in scalar multiples.
The gamma row scalings change W_o and W_2, outside BitFit's bias-translation image.
\(\operatorname{rank}(W_0\odot BA)\) reaches \(r\operatorname{rk}W_0>r\) (Prop II.9(a)); the exponential form reaches full rank, so neither embeds in LoRA\(_r\).
\(W_0\odot BA-W_0=W_0\odot(BA-J)\) has rank up to \((r+1)\operatorname{rk}W_0\), far above \(r\).
Both serve per-request adapters over one shared matmul, but the LoRAs S-LoRA serves have \(\operatorname{rank}\Delta W\le r\), while FLoRA's updates reach rank \((r+1)\operatorname{rk}W_0\).

A name clash only. Per period, Flora (Hao et al.) is the linear one-sided method \(\{W_k+XA_t\}\), with the rows of \(\Delta W\) confined to \(\mathrm{row}\,A_t\); FLoRA's \(W_0\odot BA\) has unconfined rows and a curved Hadamard image.
\((G-I)W_0\) has rank up to \(C\), so no LoRA\(_r\) with \(r<C\) simulates it.
Houlsby's correction \(U\sigma(D\,\cdot)\) lies in the \(r\)-dimensional \(\mathrm{col}\,U\); the residual adapter's full-rank linear correction \(\alpha x\) does not, for \(r<C\).

For generic \(U,D\) the edit \(y\mapsto y+U\sigma(Dy)\) is non-affine, so the realised sublayer \((\mathrm{id}+U\sigma(D\,\cdot))\circ F\) is not box-locally mergeable (Thm VI.3(c)), while LoRA's realisations keep every linear box linear.

The serial correction \(U\sigma(D\,F(x))\) reads the sublayer output, a parallel correction \(U'\sigma(D'x)\) reads its input. For a non-linear FFN \(F\) the two families are generically disjoint off \(U=0\) (the serial/parallel split of He et al.).

Pfeiffer's correction depends on \(x\) through \(\mathrm{LN}(x+F(x))\), Houlsby's FFN correction only through \(F(x)\). A width-\(r\) bottleneck of \(F(x)\) cannot recover the residual \(x\), so Houlsby generically does not reproduce Pfeiffer's functions.
Non-affine inserted box (Thm VI.3(c)); no weight of the original architecture realises it.

MAD-X composes adapters (input-independent stacking); AdapterFusion's output is, per token, a softmax-convex combination of \(V\)-projected adapter outputs. A composite \(\mathrm{TA}(\mathrm{LA}(h))\) is generically not such a combination.
The invertible adapter edits the tied input and output embeddings, which a per-layer Pfeiffer adapter never touches. So MAD-X's realisations leave Pfeiffer's image, even with LA neutral.
AdaMix deploys one adapter with input-independent weights; it cannot realise AdapterFusion's input-dependent softmax mixtures of \(N\) adapters.
LoraHub's composition weights are constants chosen post hoc (and act on weight-space LoRAs); AdapterFusion's are a function of the token, so its realisations lie outside any constant combination.

K-Adapter's features contain the full \(d\)-dimensional \(h_L\), whose values span \(\mathbb R^d\) over inputs; LST's pre-head output \(\mathrm{Up}(h^g_N)\) always lies in \(\mathrm{col}\,\mathrm{Up}\), of dimension \(\le d/r<d\) (a cut of rank \(d/r\), Thm II.10). A cut-rank argument across different codomains, so heuristic as an arrow test.
For each task Text-to-LoRA's realisation is a weight-space LoRA, which keeps every linear box linear; HyperFormer's per-task box functions are non-affine, so they lie outside T2L's image.
Compacter's \(U,D\) are sums of \(n\) Kronecker products (\(\Pi_\otimes\)); HyperFormer's generated \(U_\tau,D_\tau\) are dense, with Kronecker rank up to \(\min(m_1n_1,m_2n_2)>n\) (Thm II.11).
For non-affine \(\sigma\) the realised box \(F+sU\sigma(D\,\cdot)\) is outside \(\Phi_f(\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA})\) (Thm VI.3(c)); only \(\sigma=\mathrm{id}\) gives LoRA.
A parallel correction \(U\sigma(Dx)\) of the sublayer input is generically not a serial correction \(U'\sigma(D'F(x))\) of its output.

MAM contains a parallel adapter, yet PA is not a sub-object of it: \(f\in\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{PA}\) at \(U=0\), but no MAM parameter realises \(f\), because the prefix summand is unpointed (Thm VI.5(f)).
For \(W_o\ne0\), \(W_q\ne0\) a generic prefix's input-dependent gate \(\lambda_q\) makes the head non-affine (Thm VI.5(f)), so no weight-space realisation exists.

MAM's FFN correction is parallel, \(U\sigma(Dx)\) of the FFN input; UniPELT's only bottleneck is serial after the FFN, and its LoRA acts on \(W_q,W_v\), not on the FFN. A parallel FFN correction is generically not reproduced.
Even the LoRA summand realises the non-affine \(W_0x+\mathcal G_L(x)BAx\); with the prefix and adapter, UniPELT's realisations lie outside \(\Phi_f(\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA})\).
UniPELT's serial post-FFN correction \(U\sigma(D\,\cdot)\) of the FFN output is generically not MAM's parallel correction of the FFN input, and MAM has no LoRA on \(W_q,W_v\).

AdapterFusion trains only \(Q,K,V\) over \(N\) frozen adapters, so its realisations are softmax mixtures of fixed adapter outputs. The new averaged adapter that AdaMix trains is generically not among them; conversely, AdaMix does not route at inference.

\(f\in\mathrm{Im}\) (at \(g=0\)), but prefix tuning is unpointed (Thm VI.5(f)). Moreover LLaMA-Adapter never rescales content attention, while a prefix multiplies it by \(1-\lambda_q\) (Thm VI.5(b),(d)).
Gated extra softmax slots are non-affine in the input once the prompt has two or more tokens (generic prompts, Thm VI.5(f); one prompt token stays affine); no weight-space realisation exists.
V1 provably leaves content attention and all lower-layer computation unchanged (Thm VI.5(d)), an absolute invariant; V2's bias and scale on every linear layer break it.
Side-tuning's output contains the full-width \(B(x)\); LST's prediction sees the backbone only through ladders into a side state of width \(d/r\), a cut of rank \(d/r<d\) (Thm II.10).
A pointed arrow would send LST's base point to PA's neutral point, so both would realise \(f\); LST's base point cannot (cut-rank \(d/r\)). The same holds for every neutral-pointed extension.

The unbound prefix tuner is a separately normalised branch: its family contains \(f\) and never rescales content attention. Prefix tuning is unpointed and multiplies content weights by \(1-\lambda_q\). The 'equivalence' is empirical, not an isomorphism.

T2I-Adapter's correction \(F_c=\mathcal F_{AD}(C)\) is independent of the latent and the timestep, an invariant of its image. ControlNet's residuals depend on \(x\) through the copy, so they lie outside T2I's image.

Base-point mismatch: T2I's initial point does not realise the frozen model (no zero init), while ControlNet's does (zero convolutions). So no pointed arrow T2I \(\to\) ControlNet exists, and their injection sites differ (encoder states against skip and middle outputs).
IP-Adapter's branch keys and values are functions of the image input \(c_i\); LLaMA-Adapter's prompt keys and values are constants, so it cannot realise image-dependent branches.
\(f\in\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{AdaptFormer}\) (at \(W_{up}=0\)), but VPT's prompt tokens always take attention mass, so VPT is unpointed and cannot simulate it.
Non-affine parallel branch (Thm VI.3(c)).
PA's correction at token \(i\) depends only on \(x_i\), an invariant of its image (token locality); Convpass's depends on the \(3\times3\) grid neighbourhood.
Token mixing and non-affinity put its realisations outside \(\Phi_f(\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA})\).
Houlsby's correction is per-token; ST-Adapter's mixes neighbouring frames, so it lies outside Houlsby's image.
AIM's temporal pass re-applies the frozen attention across frames, so its realisations mix tokens over time. AdaptFormer is per-token on a frame-wise ViT and cannot reproduce them.
Mona's depthwise \(3/5/7\) convolutions mix neighbouring tokens; Houlsby's correction is per-token, an invariant of its image.
CoOp moves only the class weight vectors, so its logits stay linear functionals of the frozen normalised image embedding. CLIP-Adapter's logits are non-linear in that embedding.

CLIP-Adapter moves only the normalised image feature, so its logit vector always lies on \(\tau\,W(S^{d-1})\), the image of the unit sphere under the fixed class matrix. Tip's additive kernel term leaves that surface.
CoOp's logits stay linear in the frozen normalised image embedding; Tip adds a non-linear kernel term in that embedding.
Non-affine serial box (Thm VI.3(c)); no weight-space realisation.
\(f\in\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{ShadowPEFT}\) (at \(W_{up}=0\)), but LST's prediction passes through a width-\(d/r\) side state and can never realise \(f\) (cut-rank).
Input-dependent stateful corrections on the residual stream lie outside \(\Phi_f(\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA})\).

On length-one contexts every weight setting of a standard head (LoRA included) is affine in x, a generically prefixed head with \(W_o\ne0\), \(W_q\ne0\) is not (Thm VI.5(f)); established head-locally, whole-network containment is open.

Head-level (Thm VI.5(f)): on length-one contexts every LoRA setting is affine in x, a generically prefixed head with \(W_o\ne0\), \(W_q\ne0\) is not; whole-network non-mergeability is open (Exposé XI).

LLaMA-Adapter is pointed (g=0 reproduces f(θ0,-)), prefix tuning is unpointed, so no pointed h exists in either direction; at a layer the prefix rescales content by 1-λ_q while LLaMA-Adapter leaves content weights unchanged (Thm VI.5(c,d)).

LLaMA-Adapter is pointed at g=0, while on a head with \(W_oW_v\ne0\) every soft prompt moves the output (Thm VI.5(f)), so no pointed arrow exists either way; the two are comparable only in the unpointed slice.
CPT's reach is confined to an ε-ball around the demonstrations with label tokens frozen; unconstrained prompts leave that set.
Head-level (Thm VI.5(f)): a generic prefixed head with \(W_o\ne0\), \(W_q\ne0\) is non-affine on length-one contexts while every weight setting is affine; whole-network containment open.
Its verbalizer half is Trainable Tokens on head rows, but the prompt half makes WARP unpointed, so no pointed arrow in either direction; A5 holds only in the unpointed slice.
Its prompt varies with X through the router, so generically its realisation is not f(θ0,[P;-]) for any single P.

Its offset half is LoRA_r on a position-indexed s×d slot (a weight only for models with learned absolute position embeddings, not T5), pointed at the apex, but its prompt half is unpointed, so 'DePT = prompt + LoRA' holds only in the unpointed slice, not as a pointed arrow.
The prompt depends on M(x), so generically the realisation is not f(θ0,[P;-]) for any fixed P.
Both are zeroth-order, but MeZO moves weights from θ0 (regular base point in Meth) while BBT moves a prompt of an unpointed extension; base points and slices differ.

f(θ0) = ρ(v=0) lies in the image of visual prompting, while no VPT parameter reproduces f(θ0) (extra tokens always draw attention mass), so Im VP ⊄ Im VPT; and the pixel shift acts as an additive input change, not as new keys/values. 'Dual' lineages, not related by an arrow.

CoOp leaves the image features f(x) untouched; MaPLe always inserts vision prompts, which (being unpointed tokens) generically change f(x) for every parameter value, so 'J=1 MaPLe = CoOp' is architectural, not an arrow.
Closed-set CoOp realises x↦softmax(cos(W,f(x))/τ) with W constant; CoCoOp's rows W(x) vary with x, generically outside every fixed-head classifier.
MaPLe changes the image features through its vision prompts; CoOp only changes the class embeddings over frozen features, so MaPLe's realisations are generically outside CoOp's.
Hard top-N selection makes L2P's realisations generically discontinuous in x at selection boundaries; every ATTEMPT realisation is continuous in x (softmax router), so Im L2P ⊄ Im ATTEMPT.
Any static prefix gives a realisation continuous in x; DualPrompt's E-prompt switches with x, so its realisations are generically discontinuous at selection boundaries.
Its effect C_t(ΠĀ_i)h' decays along the sequence for stable Ā, whereas state-offset's C_th' is uniform in t; the images differ unless Ā=I.
A uniform offset C_th' is not of the decaying form C_t(ΠĀ_i)h'' for any h'' (stable Ā), so Im state-offset ⊄ Im initial-state.
(IA)^3 scales l_v⊙(W_vx+b_v) and contains no translation independent of x (unless rows of W_v vanish), so a bias shift lies outside its image.
A generic update on a fixed (1-s)mn-entry support has rank up to min(m,n), above LoRA_r's maximum rank r.

Against LoRA's default pointing (B_0=0, A_0 random; T_A stratum): S_1={BA_0} has fixed row space row A_0, which does not contain row-supported updates with arbitrary rows; the arrow above exists only into the T_B stratum.
Per stage it makes full-rank updates of every matrix in the active block; LoRA_r's maximum rank is r.
Per period LISA makes full-rank updates of its sampled layers, while GaLore's per-period update of each matrix has rank ≤ r.
(IA)^3 only rescales outputs (biases included), so an x-independent shift of a bias lies outside its image.
A \(k\)-sparse update has rank up to \(\min(k,m,n)\), so for \(k>r\) its maximum rank exceeds LoRA\(_r\)'s (conversely a generic rank-1 update is dense, O1).
The union of all \(k\)-planes is not contained in the single \(k\)-plane of one fixed mask.
A \(k\)-entry mask update can have rank up to \(\min(k,m,n)>r\).
Fisher-top supports and PaFi's data-free bottom-\(|W_0|\) supports are generically different planes, so neither image contains the other.

Concerns Child-Tuning\(_F\) only (the classified D variant has the conditional isomorphism above): fresh Bernoulli masks every step accumulate a dense update, so its reach is not inside any fixed \(k\)-plane.
Sparse updates on a 0.25-8\% support have rank far above \(r\).
On masked boxes the sparse update can have rank above \(r\).
The LoRA boxes give dense low-rank updates outside any fixed coordinate plane.

Bottom-\(|W_0|\) and top-\(|\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0)|\) supports are generically different (and nearly disjoint, though not exactly), and LIFT never trains PaFi's normalisation parameters, so PaFi's plane is not inside LIFT's reach.
A data-free magnitude support and a Fisher support are generically different planes.
A selected tile has rank up to \(l=256>r\).
SpIEL's union of strata is not contained in LT-SFT's single fixed plane.
A \(d_\phi\)-sparse update can have rank above \(r\).

For a dataset-aggregated (generically high-rank) gradient the row-wise top-\(K\) columns vary across rows and the masked update has rank up to \(\min(m,n)>r\). (For a rank-one gradient every row would select the same \(K\) columns and the rank would be at most \(K\).)
Entrywise Fisher supports generically do not contain whole columns, and whole columns are not entrywise-selected.
Top \(|g_1|\) on one batch and top \((\sum_{\rm burn\text{-}in}g)^2\) rank coordinates differently, so the two fixed planes differ.
Sparse updates can have rank above \(r\).
A HiFT stage makes full-rank updates of every matrix in the active group; a GaLore period has rank \(\le r\).
Full-rank updates on every matrix of the block exceed rank \(r\).
Same unpointed object \(M\mapsto W_0\odot M\), but Masking is pointed at \(W_0\odot M_0\ne\theta_0\) and Piggyback at \(\theta_0\): no pointed arrow either way.
Pointing defect: \(\rho(q_0)=W_0\odot M_0\ne\theta_0\), although every image point with at most \(k\) zeroed entries lies in Diff pruning's union.
Same unpointed object, different pointings (\(\mathbf 1\) versus a 5\%-masked \(M_0\)).
\(-(\mathbf 1-M)\odot W_0\) can have rank up to \(\min(m,n)>r\).
SAM ranks by \((\sum_t g_t)^2\) and FISH by \(\sum_n g_n^2\): different supports, so different planes.
Sparse updates can have rank above \(r\).
Top entries of \(\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0)\) and bottom entries of \(|W_0|\) are generically different supports (nearly, not exactly, disjoint), so LIFT's first-interval plane is not inside PaFi's plane.

Conditional: once LIFT's masks change across intervals, its accumulated \(\Delta W\) is supported on the union of the masks visited; when that union exceeds SpIEL's per-tensor budget \(d_\phi\), \(d(\mathrm{LIFT})>d(\mathrm{SpIEL})\). A single LIFT interval with \(k\le d_\phi\) is a stratum of SpIEL's union, so the obstruction is to the schedule, not to one stage.
PEQA's update \(\mathrm{diag}(\Delta s)\overline W_0\) is a row rescaling with the codes' zero pattern, QA-LoRA's is group-constant: generically the images meet only at \(\kappa\theta_0\).
Pointed at \(\kappa\theta_0\ne\theta_0\); \(\theta_0\) is generically not in its image.
\(\rho(q_0)=\kappa\theta_0\ne\theta_0\), and \(\theta_0\notin\mathrm{Im}\,\)QLoRA unless \(\operatorname{rank}e\le r\) (Prop V.2(a)): no pointed arrow either way.

With LoftQ's default single iteration both are LoRA\(_r\) over the same \(\kappa\theta_0\), but QLoRA is pointed at the apex (\(B=0\)) and LoftQ at the smooth point \(-\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)\): same image, different strata.
A generic rank-\(r\) update is not constant on quantisation groups.
Type II smooth point over \(Q\) versus QLoRA's apex at \(\kappa\theta_0\), with different apexes as well.
For \(\kappa\ne\mathrm{id}\) the apex \(Q=\kappa(W_{\rm res})\) differs from PiSSA's \(W_{\rm res}\) by a generically full-rank error, so the translated cones are not nested.
IR-QLoRA's update is a general rank-\(r\) matrix; QA-LoRA's is group-constant.
L4Q's image lies in grid families \(s\odot\tilde w+b\), QLoRA's \(\kappa\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) is off the grid: no inclusion either way.

PEQA's image is the per-row scale family on its frozen codes, \(\{\mathrm{diag}(s)\overline W_0\}\) (dim \(d_{out}\)); L4Q's is a union over code patterns of per-group scale-and-shift families. L4Q's germ is larger (per-group scales and shifts), and large PEQA rescalings would flip L4Q's recomputed codes, so neither image contains the other; the base points also differ (RTN/OPTQ versus the L4Q-init symmetric quantiser).

(IA)\(^3\) scales only \(k\), \(v\) (output) and \(W_{\rm down}\) (input) at \(\theta_0\); PEQA rescales every linear layer's output rows at \(\kappa\theta_0\) (different boxes, and O3 by the base point).
Row rescalings of the codes versus group-constant shifts: generically non-nested images.
Activation-fitted and weight-fitted quantised apexes \(Q\) differ by a generically full-rank matrix, so the translated cones are not nested.
Smooth Type II pointing over \(Q\) versus QLoRA's apex at \(\kappa\theta_0\).
Group-wise scales have \(d=d_{out}d_{in}/g>d_{out}\), so E2E-QP does not factor through per-channel PEQA.
On-grid scale families versus QLoRA's off-grid cone.

LoQT's \(B_{\rm init}\) compensates quantisation error, so \(\rho(q_0)\ne\kappa\theta_0\) (O3). Moreover the refinement re-quantises \(W_Q=q_{\rm NF4}(W-PB)\ne q_{\rm NF4}(W)\), generically by a high-rank difference, so the first-stage image \(W_Q+P_QX\) is not even inside QLoRA's \(\kappa\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) (O1); only without refinement steps is it contained, with the pointings still disagreeing.
Against a single \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) over \(\theta_0\): after \(K\ge2\) periods the reach has rank up to \(\min(Kr,m,n)>r\). (The arrow above is per period.)
Per period, a gradient-SVD frame \(P_k\) versus a random Gaussian frame \(A_t\): the period images are generically not nested.
Per period, stochastically rounded INT8 steps leave \(\mathrm{span}\,P_k\) coordinatewise, so they are not in GaLore's period image (they agree only in law); O3 also holds, by the INT8 base point.
Per period, a random Gaussian frame \(A_t\) versus a gradient-SVD frame \(P_k\): the period images are generically not nested.
A Fira step is full rank; a GaLore period has rank \(\le r\).
APOLLO's update \(G\,\mathrm{diag}(s)\) is full rank; a Flora period has rank \(\le r\).
Full-rank steps versus rank-\(\le r\) periods.
Over \(T\) steps OSD reaches \(\theta_k+\sum_tP_t\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), of dimension up to \(\min(m,Tr)\,n>rn\), so it does not factor through one GaLore period.
Adam-mini coarsens only the preconditioner, so its step is a full-rank matrix: \(d=\dim\Theta\), against \(rn\) for one GaLore period.
A MeZO step \(\lambda z_t\) has per-matrix rank \(\min(m,n)>r\), so it lies in no Flora period \(\{XA_t\}\).
For the same reason it lies in no GaLore period \(\{P_tX\}\), whose maximum rank is \(r\).
A LOMO step uses the full gradient (\(d=\dim\Theta\)); a MeZO step moves along one random line (\(d=1\)).
Factoring the second moment is not compressing the gradient. AdaLomo's step has full rank, so it lies in no Flora period \(\{XA_t\}\).

\(\theta^\star-\theta_0=\sum_i\mathrm{diag}\big(\lambda_iF_i/\textstyle\sum_j\lambda_jF_j\big)\tau_i\) has coordinate-dependent weights, so it lies outside \(\theta_0+\mathrm{span}\{\tau_i\}\) generically.
\(W^\star-W_0=\sum_i\Delta W_i\tilde G_i(\sum_j\tilde G_j)^{-1}\) right-multiplies each update by a matrix weight, so it leaves \(W_0+\mathrm{span}\{\Delta W_i\}\) generically.

Take generic modules, whose \(N^2\) products \(B_iA_j\) are linearly independent. Then LoraHub's \(\sum_{i,j}w_iw_jB_iA_j\) equals \(\sum_i\lambda_iB_iA_i\) only if \(w_iw_j=0\) for \(i\ne j\), so only one module can be active. O2 also applies: LoraHub's updates have rank \(\le r\), against up to \(\min(Nr,m,n)\) for task arithmetic.
Trimming and disjoint means act coordinatewise, so \(\tau_m\) is generically not in \(\mathrm{span}\{\tau_i\}\).
For a fixed mask, \(\sum_im_i\odot\tau_i/(1-p)\) leaves \(\mathrm{span}\{\tau_i\}\) generically. It agrees with task arithmetic only in expectation.
\(d=NL\) layer-wise coefficients, against \(N\) global ones.
Whitening mixes the tasks' singular bases, so in general \(U_\perp\Sigma V_\perp^\top\notin\mathrm{span}\{\Delta_i\}\): TSV-M is not a reweighted task arithmetic.
KnOTS-TIES trims and elects signs in the aligned \(V\)-coordinates, not in weight coordinates. So its \(\tau_m\) differs from dense TIES, and the two lines differ.
For LoRA modules, the cross terms \(B_1A_2+B_2A_1\) lie outside \(\mathrm{span}\{B_iA_i\}\).

Its functions are realised only on the adapter extension. The averaged adapter is non-affine, so it is not box-locally mergeable (Thm VI.3(c)) and generically not \(\Phi_f\) of any weight. Whole-network non-realisability is not proved (Exposé XI). So the soup does not factor through a weight-space soup over \(\Theta\).
The cross terms \(w_iw_jB_iA_j\) with \(i\ne j\) leave \(\mathrm{span}\{B_iA_i\}\).
\(d(\mathrm{CAT})=NL\) per-layer weights, against \(N\) global LoraHub weights.
For \(k<\sum r_i\) the centroids mix units from different LoRAs, so \(\Delta W\notin\mathrm{span}\{B_iA_i\}\) generically.
Per adapted matrix, \(d=2n\) merger coefficients against CAT's 2 weights.

The fused update \(W^\star-W_0=\sum_i\Delta W_iG_i(\sum_jG_j)^{-1}\) has rank \(\le\sum_ir_i\), the same bound as a sum of orthogonally adapted concepts, so rank does not separate them. Right-multiplication by \(G_i(\sum_jG_j)^{-1}\) does move the row space off any fixed frozen frame, so generically the update is not in \(\{W_0+XA_S\}\).
Despite the name, the update is additive: \(W_0+B_iA_i\) changes the Gram matrix that OFT preserves.

Composite's averaged guided noise prediction is an ensemble of \(2k\) UNet passes. Generically it is not \(\Phi_f\) of any single weight (not proved at whole-network level), so it is not in task arithmetic's image.
The mixing form is the same, but each task fibre of Poly reaches all of \(\mathcal M_{\le r}\) (\(d=r(m+n-r)\)), while LoraHub's frozen modules give an \(N\)-dimensional cone.

At equal inventory, \(d(\mathrm{MHR})-d(\mathrm{Poly})=(h-1)(S-1)(T-S)\) generically (Jacobian rank). The extra \(TS(h-1)\) logits are partly absorbed by the per-head skill-mixing and normalisation gauges. So \(d(\mathrm{MHR})>d(\mathrm{Poly})\) exactly when \(h\ge2\), \(S\ge2\) and \(T>S\), which is the multi-task regime. For \(T\le S\) the two dimensions coincide in the cases checked, and O2 does not separate them.

SMEAR's merged expert varies with the input, while AdaMix averages its experts into one fixed adapter at inference. Generically no fixed adapter of the same width realises the routed functions, so they are not in that image.

MoV variant (\((IA)^3\) experts), against \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\): per token the update \(\mathrm{diag}(\ell(x)-\mathbf 1)W_0\) has rank up to \(\min(m,n)>r\). (The MoLoRA variant is isomorphic to LoRAMoE and maps fibrewise into \(\mathrm{LoRA}_{Nr}\).)
LoRAMoE's update varies token by token, while MOELoRA's is constant per task. Per-token routing is not realised by any task-indexed weight.
The same token under two task ids receives different updates, but LoRAMoE's router sees only the token.

MoLE's input-dependent gates mix whole block outputs. So the realised functions are generically not \(\Phi_f\) of any single weight (M∞; whole-network non-realisability is generic, not proved), and they are not in LoraHub's weight-space image.

The block output jumps when the second- and third-ranked experts swap: the weights agree at the tie, but the selected expert changes. So for generic trained experts MixLoRA's functions are discontinuous in the input. LoRAMoE mixes inside each linear layer with an everywhere-positive softmax, so its functions are continuous. Hence MixLoRA's routed functions are not in LoRAMoE's image.
Token-dependent scalings give functions that generically no single weight realises (M∞). So they are not in LoraHub's static weight-space image.
HydraLoRA's update changes token by token within one task, while MOELoRA's is constant for a task id, so per-token routing is not realised by any task-indexed weight.

Arrow's paper composition \((\sum_ip_iB_i)(\sum_ip_iA_i)\) has cross terms \(p_ip_jB_iA_j\). A top-2 PHATGOOSE update \(w_1B_1A_1+w_2B_2A_2\) with both weights positive would need \(p_1p_2=0\), so for a generic library it lies outside Arrow's per-token image.

Top-\(k\) routing makes PHATGOOSE's functions discontinuous in the input at ranking ties. X-LoRA's default dense softmax scalings vary continuously with the hidden states, so for generic experts PHATGOOSE's functions are not in that X-LoRA image (X-LoRA's optional top-\(k\) mode is not covered by this argument).
For \(k\ge2\) the paper's per-token weight contains cross terms \(p_ip_jB_iA_j\) (\(i\ne j\)) outside \(\mathrm{span}\{B_zA_z\}\), which contains every PHATGOOSE per-token update.
Arrow's weights change per token and per layer, so its realised functions are generically not \(\Phi_f\) of one weight. LoraHub's single global \(w\) gives one static weight.

Retrieval is piecewise constant in the prompt, so for generic libraries the realised functions jump at retrieval boundaries. X-LoRA's default dense softmax scalings vary continuously and never vanish, so that mode cannot reproduce them (X-LoRA's optional top-\(k\) mode is not covered by this argument).

Even with a constant gate, LoRA-Flow's update \(\sum_iw_iB_iA_i\) (\(w\) in the open simplex) would need LoraHub's cross terms to vanish, which for a generic library forces a single nonzero weight. With a token-dependent gate its functions are not \(\Phi_f\) of any one weight.
The same prompt from two tenants is served with two different adapters, but an input-routed mixture sees only the tokens.

Punica's family is indexed by tenants, so the same prompt from two tenants is served with two different adapters. X-LoRA's scalings are computed from the tokens alone, so in any mode it gives the same prompt the same scalings; with its default dense softmax they are also strictly positive on every adapter, so for linearly independent adapters it never serves exactly one of them.

LiDB's row spaces sweep the \(a\)-dimensional \(\mathrm{row}\,P_{in}\) (any vector of it at \(r=1\)), while VeRA's updates \(\Lambda_bB\Lambda_dA\) keep their rows in the fixed \(\mathrm{row}\,A\). With independent frames \(\mathrm{row}\,P_{in}\not\subseteq\mathrm{row}\,A\).

MOELoRA's task updates \(\sum_i\omega_{\tau i}B_iA_i\) all have column space in \(\mathrm{col}[B_1\cdots B_N]\) and row space in \(\mathrm{row}[A_1;\dots;A_N]\), both \(r\)-dimensional. T2L's \(B(z)\) varies with the task, so two tasks can need more than \(r\) column directions.
D2L's per-input rank \(rK\) grows with document length, while T2L's generated adapters have rank at most \(r\), so long inputs exceed T2L's maximum rank.
\(d(\text{Tina})=r(m+n-r)\) per adapted matrix with \(r=32\), far above TinyLoRA's \(u\)-dimensional linear image, although both papers argue that RL needs few parameters.

Different quantisers give different translates of the same cone: \(\kappa_{\rm NVFP4}\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\subseteq\kappa_{\rm NF4}\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) forces \(\kappa_{\rm NVFP4}\theta_0=\kappa_{\rm NF4}\theta_0\). The two are related by a translation, a transport rather than an arrow.
\(\theta_0\notin\kappa\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) unless \(\mathrm{rank}\,e\le r\) (Prop V.2(a)), and the translate lies inside \(\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) only if \(e=0\).

\(S_1(\text{PLoP})=\{XA_0\}\) has dimension \(mr\) per adapted matrix, while AdaLoRA at \(\Lambda=0\) has \(\dim S_1=r\) (VIII.B). \(S_1\) is monotone along pointed arrows (Obs I.6), so there is no pointed arrow, although both allocate budget across modules.
\(d(\text{LoRI})=|M|\), about \(3.2\,d_{out}\) per matrix at \(s=0.9\), \(r=32\), exceeds VeRA's \(d=d_{out}+r-1\), although both rest on frozen random projections.

Once the ramp ends, \(\rho(q_0)-\theta_0=\frac\alpha rA_0A_0^\top\ne0\), so SingLoRA lies in none of LoRA's standard strata and there is no pointed arrow into LoRA at \((0,A_0)\); the arrow above lives in the unpointed slice.
SHINE writes rank-8 updates into every linear layer of each block, D2L only into the MLP down-projections. A SHINE context with a nonzero attention, gate or up update is outside D2L's image.
GenerativeAdapter's per-context update on \(W_o\) has rank 128; SHINE's generated adapters have rank 8.

GenerativeAdapter writes only into the attention output projections and D2L only into the MLP down-projections, and GenerativeAdapter's normalised update is never zero, so for generic contexts their images do not meet.

GOAT's top-\(k\) routed functions jump at ranking ties, while HydraLoRA's dense softmax gives functions continuous in the input. So generic GOAT functions are outside HydraLoRA's image (its main baseline).
With TIES inside, trimming and sign election act in different coordinates (core frames from stacked factors, KnOTS's frame from concatenated updates), so the two merged lines differ.
At one timestep K-LoRA uses the content LoRA in some layers and the style LoRA in others. Task arithmetic's global coefficients cannot select per layer, so that weight is outside its image.

Under full bidirectional attention, OminiControl's condition-token states depend on the noisy latent; EasyControl's causal mutual mask makes them functions of the condition alone. Generic OminiControl functions are therefore outside EasyControl's image (generic, not proved at network level).

EasyControl blocks condition-to-content attention while keeping content-to-condition. OminiControl's bias \(\log\gamma\) acts symmetrically on both \(X\leftrightarrow C\) blocks and its condition tokens see the latent, so generic EasyControl functions are outside its image (generic, not proved at network level).
Top-1 routing switches experts at ties, so ICEdit's functions are discontinuous in the input. LoRAMoE's dense softmax mixture is continuous, so generic ICEdit functions are outside its image.
An SD-LoRA stage also re-weights every earlier direction, so \(d=r(m+n-r)+(t-1)\), while an O-LoRA stage is a single LoRA\(_r\) with earlier components frozen, \(d=r(m+n-r)\).
One step updates \(t\) rows of a \(d_v=1024\) table, an update of rank up to \(\min(t,d_v)\) (500 on TriviaQA), above a rank-\(r\) LoRA on the same table.
SEAL's inner updates have rank 64 (knowledge incorporation) or 128 (ARC) per matrix, while SHINE's generated adapters have rank 8.

At its neutral point LoReFT maps to \((R_0^\top,0)\), with \(S_1=\{R_0^\top Y\}\): the \(\mathrm T_B\) stratum. Standard LoRA is pointed in \(\mathrm T_A\) (\(S_1=\{XA_0\}\)), so there is no pointed arrow into it.
RED's edit \(h\mapsto\ell\odot h+b\) is diagonal and acts at every position. LoReFT's rank-\(r\) edit is non-diagonal and position-selective, so its functions lie outside RED's image.
LoRA on \(W_{q,k,v,o}\) keeps the embedding and the norm gains at \(\theta_0\), while LongLoRA moves them, so its image is not in any LoRA\(_{qkvo}\) image.

The paper's 'LoRA+' (LoRA \(\oplus\) embedding \(\oplus\) norms) is unrelated to Hayou et al.'s LoRA+, which has LoRA's image (only the \(B/A\) learning-rate ratio differs). The embedding and gain summands lie outside that image.
Each O-LoRA stage is a full LoRA\(_r\), with \(d=r(m+n-r)\), while an InfLoRA stage is LoRA-FA\((A_t)\) with \(d=rm\), so O-LoRA stages do not factor through InfLoRA's.
Each InfLoRA stage is pointed at \(\theta_{t-1}\) (\(B_t=0\)), while SD-LoRA's normalisation forces a unit-norm offset at the start of every task, so no pointed arrow maps one stage into the other.

Textual inversion is pointed: \(v_0=E_w\) reproduces the prompt with the word \(w\). A soft prompt always draws attention mass, and on a head with \(W_oW_v\ne0\) it has no neutral value (Thm VI.5(f)). The base-point strata differ, so there is no pointed arrow either way.
Dense \(W^k,W^v\) updates reach rank \(\min(d_{\rm out},d_{\rm text})>r\). The paper finds low-rank training worse; only post-hoc SVD compression comes close.
SVDiff keeps \(W_0\)'s singular frames, an absolute invariant; dense K/V updates move them.
Each selected expert gets a dense update of rank up to \(\min(d,d_{ff}^{(e)})>r\).

ESFT trains a few experts in every MoE layer at once, on a fixed support. A LISA stage trains only \(\gamma\) sampled layers (all experts in them) plus embeddings and head. So, when \(\gamma\) is below the number of MoE layers, no single stage contains ESFT's image. (That ESFT never touches the embeddings blocks only the converse LISA \(\to\) ESFT.)

WiSE-FT moves along \(W_0+\alpha\Delta W\), shrinking the whole update toward \(\theta_0\). Intruder reduction moves along \(W_1+(\lambda-1)\sigma_ju_jv_j^\top\). The two lines meet only at \(W_1\), unless \(\Delta W\) is itself the intruder component.
CODA's prompt varies continuously with \(x\), while L2P's is piecewise constant (hard top-\(N\) retrieval). So generic CODA realisations are not L2P realisations.
A static prefix is a single point. CODA's prefix depends on \(x\) through \(q(x)\), so its realisations are generically not those of any single prefix.
The target is the full rank-\(r\) cone, \(d=r(m+n-r)\). LoRA-X's target is confined to frozen singular subspaces, with \(d=r\) (or \(r^2\)). So a Trans-LoRA output is generically not a LoRA-X point.

At LoRA's default pointing \((0,A_0)\), \(S_1=\{XA_0\}\) has the random row space \(\mathrm{row}A_0\), which does not contain LoRA-X's directions \(u_iv_i^\top\). The arrow exists only into the \(\mathrm T_B\) stratum.
LoReFT edits the residual stream only at selected positions (M∞); LoFiT shifts head outputs at every position. A position-uniform shift lies outside LoReFT's realisations, and conversely.
At FLoRA's default zero-core pointing, \(S_1=\{U_0XV_0^\top\}\) has dimension \(r^2\), against MoSLoRA's \(mr\). \(S_1\) is not contained, so there is no pointed arrow at the default pointings.
Every GLoRA path is a weight-space reparametrisation (M1), so its realisations lie in \(\Phi_f(\Theta)\). NOAH's VPT tokens and non-linear adapter leave that set (Thm VI.3(c), VI.5(f)).

NOAH's LoRA on \(W_q,W_k\) changes every token's queries and keys. AutoPEFT has no module there: its adapters sit at the FFN and its prefixes only add key/value slots, so neither reproduces a generic low-rank change of the attention logits. (The VPT-Deep part alone would not obstruct, since a deep prompt acts at its layer as a constrained K/V prefix; the LoRA summand does.)

AutoPEFT's serial post-FFN adapter reads \(F(x)\), and a generic ReLU function of \(F(x)\) is not reproduced by MAM's parallel FFN adapter (which reads \(x\)) plus a key/value prefix (as for UniPELT vs MAM). Separately, the converse also fails: MAM's sizes (prefix length 30, fixed scaling) are not points of AutoPEFT's grid.
ReLU adapters and prefixes are non-affine inserted boxes (Thm VI.3(c)); no weight of the original architecture realises them.

BLoB's samples \(W_0+BA\) keep the trained \(\mathrm{col}\,B\), since \(B\) is deterministic. Laplace samples perturb \(B\) as well and change the column space, so the Laplace posterior's support is not contained in BLoB's.
Pruned groups contribute the update \(-\mathrm{diag}(\mathbf 1-m)W_0\), whose rank, up to the number of pruned rows, exceeds \(r\).
Over a common \(\kappa\theta_0\), ModuLoRA sits at the apex (\(B=0\)) and LoftQ at the smooth point \(-\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)\): same image, different strata.
QA-LoRA's updates are constant on quantisation groups. ModuLoRA's generic \(BA\) is not, so its image is not contained.
\(BA+S\) is full rank w.h.p., so \(\rho_{\max}>r\).
A parallel adapter is pointed at \(U=0\). MEFT's fixed coupling scalar \(\lambda=0.1\) leaves no exactly neutral value, so the two lie in different base-point strata.
Non-linear adapters inside a two-stream coupling are non-affine inserted boxes (Thm VI.3(c)); no weight of the original architecture realises them.
Selected matrices get dense full-rank updates, so \(\rho_{\max}>r\).

Spectrum's fixed support spans matrices in many layers, chosen per module type. A LISA stage trains \(\gamma\) whole sampled layers, so no single stage contains Spectrum's image, and Spectrum never resamples.
PiSSA is a Type II object (a smooth point of a translated cone); LoRA-Dash sits at the apex of an untranslated cone. The strata differ, and the images are incomparable.
Against \(\mathrm{LoRA}_r\) at equal rank: \(\rho_{\max}=r+s>r\).
PEM addition merges factors, so its result has rank \(\le r\); LCM-LoRA's sum of products reaches rank \(r'+r\). Conversely, PEM's cross terms \(B'A_{\rm LCM}\) leave LCM-LoRA's span.

For the training object O2 already applies (\(d=r(m+n-r)>1\)). Even on its deployed line, a slider's strength ranges over \(\mathbb R\) (negative values erase a concept). WiSE-FT's \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) gives a segment whose germ at \(\theta_0\) is a half-line. The converse arrow exists when \(\theta_1-\theta_0=BA\).

OminiControl's LoRA acts only on condition tokens, a position-selective edit (M∞ by Thm VI.3(a)), so its noise and text tokens always pass through \(W_0\). IC-LoRA's position-uniform \(W_0+BA\) on every token lies outside its realisations.
A soup averages fine-tuned endpoints with weights summing to 1 and never returns \(\theta_0\). WiSE-FT's segment contains \(\theta_0\) and every \(\theta_0+\alpha\tau\).

LP-FT's second stage is Full FT, so its reach is all of \(\Theta\) (\(d=\dim\Theta\)); WiSE-FT is a segment (\(d=1\)). In addition the base points differ: LP-FT's FT stage is pointed at \((v_{\rm lp},B_0)\), WiSE-FT's family at the zero-shot point.
\(\{BA_0\}\) has a fixed row space and MiCA's \(\{U_{\min}Y\}\) a fixed column space; neither contains the other.
HetLoRA's zero-padded factor average has rank \(\le r_{\max}\); FLoRA's stacked aggregate reaches rank \(\sum_kr_k\).
\(d(\mathrm{LoRA}_{r})=r(m+n-r)>mr=d(\mathrm{FFA})\): HetLoRA's trainable \(A\) leaves the fixed row space.
The lite-residual weights add dimensions outside the bias space: \(d(\mathrm{TinyTL})>d(\mathrm{BitFit})\).

Both target activation memory, but LST's side network is an unpointed extension: its initial realisation is not the frozen network's. TinyTL is a coordinate block of the pretrained network pointed at \(\kappa\theta_0\) (the 8-bit base), so the base points differ and no pointed arrow exists.

BBT reaches the random affine subspace \(p_0+\mathrm{col}A\) of dimension \(k\ll\ell d\). Apart from \(p_0\) itself (when \(p_0\) is drawn from the vocabulary), it generically contains no tuple of vocabulary rows, which are exactly AutoPrompt's points.

At function level the realised map (adapted prompt KV cache, frozen decode weights) is not Phi_f of any single weight for generic prompts, so no weight-space LoRA lifts it (M-infinity). On each prompt position the update is still a LoRA update.

Complementary gates on the same LoRA update. For a fixed invocation position aLoRA leaves the prompt before t_inv at W_0 and adapts later tokens; PreFT adapts the prompt and leaves every generated token at W_0. For generic prompts neither family of realised maps contains the other.

For N >= 2 OFT experts with generic generators, W_0(C(Q_m)^T - I) is not in span{W_0(C(Q_i)^T - I)}, because the Cayley map is not linear. Conversely task arithmetic's family leaves the K_out level set that OrthoMerge's output keeps.

Same top-r subspace, but RLPO is a Type I apex (B_0 = 0, W_0 unsplit) and PiSSA a Type II smooth point: different strata, incomparable images at equal rank (Thm II.2(d)).

Per token both have the form (mixture of heads) times a shared A, but LiME's confidence-adaptive top-k (theta = 0.7) and n-gram windows switch experts discontinuously, while HydraLoRA's dense softmax gates are continuous in the token. So for generic trained parameters LiME's routed functions are not HydraLoRA's (the MixLoRA argument).

Per step, AGZO's direction R U^T has rank <= r on every linear layer, while MeZO's Gaussian direction has full rank almost surely. So the step lines differ, and AGZO's line is not in MeZO's. Read in law: the rank-<=r directions form a measure-zero set that MeZO's Gaussian direction hits with probability 0.

Checked numerically.

BLoB's samples keep the trained col B, since its B is deterministic. Bayesian-LoRA samples B as well, so its posterior support leaves every fixed FB(B) slice.
FFA-LoRA's updates keep the fixed row space row A_0; FLoRG's row space row(AR) moves with A, so its image is not inside FFA-LoRA's.

InfLoRA's frame lies in an approximate null space of old-task inputs; LoDA's isolated frame maximises a new-to-old energy ratio and its shared frame is excited by old tasks. For generic data the stage images are not nested.

The same context token is served with a different head for each agent role, while HydraLoRA's softmax router is a function of the token alone and never exactly one-hot: tenant indexing is not token routing.
Different points of the S stratum (masked-SVD P against weight-SVD P) give translated cones with different vertices, hence incomparable images (Thm II.2(a),(d)).
Target instance: LoRA_r at the T_A apex. At equal rank, a Type II smooth point against LoRA's Type I apex.
LoCO (n = 1) is exactly orthogonal and keeps K_out; OFTv2's Cayley-Neumann images leave the K_out level set, so near theta_0 the two images meet only at theta_0.

A Type II smooth start over Q against QLoRA's apex at kappa theta_0, with different apexes as well (as LQ-LoRA).

HyperDreamBooth's fibres lie in W_0 + P_out M_{<=r} P_in with frozen random frames, so their row spaces stay in row P_in. Prompt2Effect generates dense factors whose row spaces range over all of R^{d_in}.
Both fix their row space, GiVA at row V_r^T (a gradient frame) and VeRA at row A (a random frame). For generic data the two row spaces differ.
LoRA-SB's updates B R A keep col B fixed; GiVA's column space Gamma col B moves with gamma.
f(theta_0) is AP's value at delta = 0, while no VPT parameter reproduces f (extra tokens always draw attention mass), so Im AP is not inside Im VPT.

LayerNorm shifts are shared across positions; a position-specific delta at one layer is not a (gamma, beta) edit. Prop. 1's matching needs a position-uniform delta, unit effective scale and batch-invariant statistics.
d(LoRA_r) = r(m+n-r) > mr = d(LoRA-FA): shrinking A early does not freeze it.

The frozen backbone function (pretrained norm parameters, with the same head on both sides) is in Im MDPD, while LST is unpointed: its side network's up-projection has rank <= d/r, so no LST parameter reproduces it. So Im MDPD is not inside Im LST. LST also keeps its side network at inference.

Different points of stratum S: LOI's vertex W_0 - alpha U_{1:r}V_{r+1:2r}^T against LoRA-GA's W_0 - P_GA with P_GA proportional to U_{r+1:2r}V_{1:r}^T (the paper's own Thm 5.1 contains both; it uses the mirrored member). Translated cones with distinct vertices are not nested (Thm II.2(a),(d)).
LOI instance: a smooth Type II start against LoRA's T_A apex at equal rank, so the images are incomparable (Thm II.2(d)). The paper's zero-init variant is LoRA itself (h = id).

At equal block size b a POET-X round has d = (b-1)(d_in+d_out)/2 skew parameters on both sides, against OFTv2's d_in(b-1)/2 on the input side. OFTv2 maps into a round (freeze P at I, A2), not conversely.
Per stage, P^T W R^T - W has rank up to min(m,n) for generic block-orthogonal factors, while a ReLoRA stage update has rank at most r.

MixLoRA routes experts only on the FFN and puts static, input-independent LoRAs on q, k, v, o. LoRA-Mixer's token-dependent updates on the attention projections are therefore generically not MixLoRA realisations (and LoRA-Mixer leaves the FFN frozen).
Token-dependent gates give functions that generically no single weight realises (M-infinity), so they are not in LoraHub's static weight-space image (as for MoLE and X-LoRA).

Doc-to-LoRA generates one static update per document, the same at every position; In-Place TTT's W_down changes from chunk to chunk inside a document, so for generic contexts its position-dependent realised map is not that of any per-document weight.
Per step FZOO's slice span{u_1,...,u_N} has d = N > 1 = d(MeZO step line). For N = 1 the step line is a Rademacher line, which a Gaussian line meets only at theta_t almost surely (O1).

LoRAMoE's softmax weights are strictly positive and its experts sit on the FFN only. LD-MoLE's Sparsegen weights vanish exactly on open sets of tokens and its experts also edit the attention projections; for generic experts (linearly independent B_iA_ix) equal realised functions would force equal weights, so its sparse routings are not LoRAMoE realisations.
Over a cycle every atom moves in both factors, so d(AR1-ZO) = r(m+n-r) > mr = d(LoRA-FA).
For T >= 2 and generic adapters, gamma S sum_t B_tA_t leaves span{B_tA_t}: S mixes the shared output directions, so Pico-TA is not a reweighted task arithmetic.

FourierFT's image is spanned by a few real 2-D cosine patterns cos(2 pi (j x/d_out + l y/d_in)) at sampled frequencies (rank 2 each, point-symmetric); FrameFT's atoms are rank-one products of realified (d/2)-point DFT vectors on each side, block-diagonal in frequency. A rank-one atom would need both (j,l) and (j,-l) sampled at matching frequencies, so for generic supports Im FrameFT is not contained in Im FourierFT.
The maximum rank reaches n_c (block-diagonal core), far above r at matched budgets.
f lies in Im PMT (at M = 0) but not in Im prefix tuning, which is unpointed (Thm VI.5(f)); moreover a prefix multiplies content attention by 1 - lambda_q, which PMT never does.
For generic M the branch is non-affine in the input (elu or gelu), while every LoRA setting keeps the attention projections linear, so no weight-space LoRA realises it (Thm VI.3(c)).

The catalogued parallel adapter is He et al.'s ReLU bottleneck, whose branch U ReLU(D x) is piecewise linear in its input. PMT's branch sum_h W_O^(h) M_h^T phi(W_Q^(h) x) with phi = elu or gelu is real-analytic and non-affine on open sets of (normalised) inputs, so for generic M it equals no finite ReLU branch: Im PMT is not inside Im PA. PMT factors only through a phi-activated parallel branch with a frozen down-projection W_Q, which is not a catalogued object (the parallel-adapter entry excludes GELU-bottleneck arrows for the same reason).

Different quantisers give different translates of the same cone: Q(R) + L_stab and NF4(W_0) differ by a generically full-rank matrix, and c + M_{<=r} lies in c' + M_{<=r} only if c = c' (proof of Thm II.2(a)). The activation quantisers differ as well (A4 against A16).
rho(q_0) = Q(R) + L_stab != theta_0, and theta_0 is not in the image unless rank e <= r (Prop V.2(a)): no pointed arrow.

When the mask keeps part but not all of the support of tau_A, m (.) tau_A is not a multiple of tau_A, so the line differs from task arithmetic's theta_B + lambda tau_A (which stays near zero-shot across bases, as the paper reports).
A rank-r start that compensates the quantisation error (a smooth point over W~_C) against QLoRA's apex at kappa theta_0, with different apexes as well (as LQ-LoRA).
Piggyback's masks are {0,1}-valued, so its image keeps every sign of W_0; a ternary mask flips the signs of nonzero weights (about 26% of weights flip in the paper's transition analysis).

(A (x) B - 11^T)) carries the generic zero/sign pattern of W_tern, so its Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement has rank > 1 (checked: 6 for the same split, 4 for another), while LoKr's update C (x) BA is a single Kronecker term (rearrangement rank 1). Hence Im ternary is not inside Im LoKr. (Conversely LoKr can create entries where W_0 is zero, which the zero-locking ternary action cannot.)

TIES trims and elects signs coordinatewise in weight coordinates; AdaRank keeps or prunes whole singular triplets. Their merged vectors differ generically.
Each SLAO stage trains both factors, d = r(m+n-r), while an InfLoRA stage is LoRA-FA(A_t) with d = rm.
The projected, per-head rescaled vector generically leaves span{Delta_I}: Delta_I(I - P_H) is a multiple of Delta_I only if Delta_I already annihilates the marker inputs.

MoLE gives every rank-one atom of a library LoRA the same weight G_n(x); MoRE weights the atoms of one LoRA independently and sparsely. For generic libraries (linearly independent atoms b_m a_m^T x) its realisations are not MoLE's.

For r > 2 and W_theta != 0 an expert output contains sin(theta_i(x)) ||A_ix|| e_{2,i}(x), which is not differentiable on {A_ix = 0}; MixLoRA's realisations are analytic on each routing cell (softmax gate times linear experts), so generic RotMoLE functions are not MixLoRA's. MixLoRA's routed experts also sit on the FFN, RotMoLE's on q, k, v, o.
Per stage ScaLoRA restarts at a smooth split point and ReLoRA at the apex (B = 0): different strata, so the stage images are incomparable at equal rank (Thm II.2(d)).
After K re-splits ScaLoRA's cumulative update can reach rank min((K+1)r, m, n) (measured: 54 at r = 4), while Delta-LoRA's total update has rank at most 2r.
The maximum rank min(d_in, d_out) exceeds r.
At equal N, d(DiaBlo) = d_in d_out / N exceeds MELoRA's sum over blocks of (r/N)(d_in/N + d_out/N - r/N); MELoRA maps into DiaBlo (factor each block), not conversely.
Group-wise scales have d = d_out d_in / g > d_out, so the GPTQ instance does not factor through per-channel PEQA (as EfficientQAT).

QZO's start GPTQ(W_0) (on-grid codes with fitted scales) differs from QLoRA's vertex NF4(W_0) by a generically full-rank matrix, so it is not in NF4(W_0) + M_{<=r}: Im QZO is not inside Im QLoRA (as EfficientQAT -/-> QLoRA).

PERK writes rank-256 updates into every linear module (the top 4 layers at 7B/8B), Doc-to-LoRA only into the MLP down-projections; a PERK context with a nonzero attention update is outside Doc-to-LoRA's image.
L2P's prompts are piecewise constant in x (hard top-N retrieval from a pool), while VAPT's vary continuously with the block's tokens, so generic VAPT realisations are not L2P's (as for CODA-Prompt).
AdaPaD starts at a nonzero rank-1 point (rho(q_0) != theta_0, S_1 = {x a_1^T + b_1 y^T} of dimension m + n - 1 per module), AdaLoRA at Lambda = 0 with dim S_1 = r: no pointed arrow.
Same image, but rho(q_0) != theta_0: h = id is only a weak morphism, and the start is a rank-r smooth point rather than the apex (as LoRA-One).
LoRA-GA subtracts its initial adapter (vertex W_0 - P_GA); LoRA-DA does not (vertex W_0). The two cones are incomparable, as in Thm II.2(d).
PiSSA keeps the residual W_0 - [W_0]_r (vertex W_0 - [W_0]_r); WASI drops it (vertex 0). Translated cones with distinct vertices are not nested.

Im WASI = M_{<=K}; a generic X of rank K has X - W_0 of rank min(m,n) > r (checked), so X is not in W_0 + M_{<=r} = Im LoRA and Im WASI is not inside Im LoRA. WASI's start is also not theta_0 (truncation defect), so no pointed arrow either.
Default instance (R_n = I_n): updates reach full rank (measured near full rank in every layer), above LoRA_r's maximum rank r.
Selected modules receive dense updates of rank up to min(m,n) > 16.

Spectral flattening (LoRA inputs) and the block mask move the merged delta out of span{Delta_i}.

TSV-M puts each task's own Sigma_i in its diagonal block of the whitened basis; DC-Merge puts the merged cover coordinates there, including cross-task contributions inside each block, so the merged deltas differ.

aLoRA keeps every token before the invocation position at W_0; MaLoRA's gate is strictly positive on prompt tokens, so for generic prompts its realisations are not aLoRA's. With the invocation at the first token aLoRA is one static LoRA, which cannot reproduce MaLoRA's token-varying lambda_t BA.
